remarks: This session's outbound HTTPS goes through a shared, policy-enforcing egress proxy. Several candidate .gov.in/.nic.in hosts (e.g. cglabour.nic.in, services.india.gov.in) consistently returned 'CONNECT tunnel failed, response 502' (connect_rejected) on every retry, which the proxy documentation attributes either to the destination host not being permitted for this session or to the host genuinely being unreachable/non-resolving; other .nic.in/.gov.in hosts (e.g. cghealth.nic.in, dgfasli.gov.in, labour.gov.in) resolved and returned normal 200 responses in the same session, so the failures are host-specific rather than a blanket proxy policy against the TLD.

The strongest lead for Chhattisgarh's actual Factory-License-relevant single-window system (invest.cg.gov.in, Single Window System 2.0, launched July 2024) was discovered not via a search snippet but by fetching csidc.in directly and reading its own outbound link — however it could not be added to verifiedSources because curl cannot complete TLS verification against it (broken/incomplete certificate chain), and per the session's rules TLS verification was not disabled to work around this.

No reachable, independently-verifiable copy of the Chhattisgarh Factories Rules, 1962 (or its 2023/2025/2026 amendments) was found this session — only secondary commentary (law-firm/compliance blogs) describes them. The primary candidate official sources for this text (a Chhattisgarh Labour Department site and egazette.gov.in) were both unreachable/unverifiable, as detailed in `excluded`.

Several third-party consultancy/aggregator sources (taxguru.in, indiafilings.com, professionalutilities.com, etc.) surfaced useful leads on the process and domain names during search, but per the spec none of them were used as sources themselves — only the government URLs they pointed to were tested, and most of those could not be independently verified this session.
